Part 2&3 物品 OBJECTS

Describe a new law you would like to introduce in your country

描述一项你想在国内推行的新法律

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a new law you would like to introduce in your country

  • What law it is (是什么法律)
  • What changes this law brings (这项法律带来什么变化)
  • Whether this new law will be popular (这项新法会不会受欢迎)
  • How you came up with the new law (你是怎么想出这项新法的)
  • And explain how you feel about this new law (并解释你对这项新法的感受)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a new law you would like to introduce in your country

The law I'd like to introduce is one that guarantees workers two full rest days every week, which people often call the double rest day policy. In my country, many companies already promise weekends off on paper, but in reality employees still receive work messages and tasks on Saturdays and Sundays, so the law would make it illegal for employers to contact staff about work during those two days. As for the changes it would bring, I think the biggest one is that people would finally have proper time to recover. They could spend weekends with their families, take up hobbies, or simply sleep in, which would improve both their physical and mental health in the long run. Would it be popular? I believe so, at least among ordinary workers. Most of my friends complain about working overtime, so I'm fairly confident a law like this would be welcomed. Of course, some companies might resist it, because they rely on employees being available all the time. I came up with this idea after seeing a news report about a young man who collapsed from overwork. It really struck me that rest is not a luxury, it's a basic right. Honestly, I feel quite strongly about this law. To me, it's not just about having free time, it's about respecting people's lives outside work.

我想推行的新法是保障双休落地，强制企业保证员工每周两天完整休息；会带来生活质量的提升，普通上班族会欢迎，但企业可能抵触；灵感来自过劳新闻，我认为休息是基本权利。

Q2What rules should students follow at school?

I think the most essential rules are about respect and safety. Students should respect their teachers and classmates, which means no bullying and no disruptive behavior in class. They should also follow basic safety rules, like not running in the corridors or leaving school without permission. Having said that, I don't think schools should be too strict, because some freedom helps students develop independence. On the whole, rules should create a safe environment without killing creativity.

学校规则核心是尊重与安全：尊重师生、不欺凌、守安全规则；但不宜过严，要给自由发展空间。

Q3Do people in your country usually obey the law?

Generally speaking, I'd say most people in my country obey the law in their daily lives, like following traffic rules and paying taxes. However, there are some gray areas, for example, jaywalking or minor parking violations are quite common, because people don't see them as serious. I think this comes down to enforcement, when people believe they won't be caught, they tend to take shortcuts. That said, for major laws, like criminal ones, the vast majority of people follow them without question.

多数人日常守法（交通、纳税），但闯红灯、乱停车等灰色地带常见，因为觉得不会被抓；重大法律基本人人遵守。

Q4What kinds of behavior are considered as good behavior?

I think good behavior generally means actions that show respect for others and for society. For example, being polite, helping people in need, and following public rules are all widely considered good. In my country, there's also a strong emphasis on filial piety, so taking care of elderly parents is seen as very admirable. Of course, what counts as good behavior can vary across cultures, but I believe the core idea is the same, treating others the way you'd like to be treated.

好行为=尊重他人与社会：礼貌、助人、守公共规则；中国还强调孝道，照顾父母很受尊敬；文化不同但核心相同。

Q5Do you think children can learn about the law outside of school?

Absolutely, I think children can learn a lot about the law outside school, and in many ways it's more effective. For instance, parents can explain simple rules at home, like why we shouldn't take things that don't belong to us. Also, everyday experiences teach children about rules, such as waiting in line or following traffic lights. I mean, real-life situations make the law feel relevant, whereas school lessons can seem abstract. So I'd say family and daily life play a huge role in legal education.

完全可以，而且更有效：父母在家讲简单规则，日常排队、看红绿灯都是法律教育；真实情境比课堂更贴近生活。

Q6What are the benefits for people to obey rules?

I think the benefits are both personal and social. On a personal level, obeying rules keeps people safe and helps them avoid trouble, like fines or accidents. On a social level, when everyone follows the same rules, society runs more smoothly, for example, traffic flows better when drivers respect the signals. There's also a sense of fairness, because rules protect everyone equally. So on the whole, following rules isn't just about restriction, it actually creates order and trust, which benefit everybody.

个人层面保安全、免麻烦；社会层面秩序更顺、更公平；守规则创造秩序与信任，人人受益。

Q7How can parents teach children to obey rules?

I believe the most effective way is to lead by example. Children learn more from what their parents do than from what they say, so if parents always follow rules themselves, kids are likely to copy that behavior. Parents can also explain the reasons behind rules in simple language, rather than just saying 'because I told you so'. Another useful approach is to give children small responsibilities, like tidying their own toys, which teaches them that rules create order. Consistency is key, I think.

最有效是言传身教，孩子模仿父母；用简单语言解释规则背后的原因；给孩子小责任（收拾玩具）培养规则意识；坚持一致。
